title: Keeping AI test runs out of player counts in a browser card game
author: Fluffy-Play1251
selftext:
I'm building Aether Vanguard, a free browser card game, with AI-assisted code and narrative text and AI-generated visual assets. One awkward part of having agents test the game is that a successful test run can also look like a new player.



The telemetry now separates signed QA activity from unclassified production activity. Opening the game, reaching the match screen, starting a match and making an accepted manual game action are different events. The daily acquisition count uses the last of those, with persistent installation IDs and server receipt time, rather than treating a screen change as play.



That still doesn't prove a human showed up. Unsigned internal visits, bots, cleared browser storage and multiple devices remain unresolved. Today's report has one first-known engaged installation; calling that one verified new player would overstate what we know.



The game is six turns, and you win by taking two of three lanes. Guest play needs no account or download, and real-money purchases are unavailable: [https://theredwizard.net/aethervanguard/](https://theredwizard.net/aethervanguard/)



If you try a match, was it clear by turn two which lanes you wanted to win? The short first-match guide is here: [https://thereddestwizard.itch.io/aether-vanguard/devlog/1678187/your-first-aether-vanguard-match-choose-two-lanes-to-win](https://thereddestwizard.itch.io/aether-vanguard/devlog/1678187/your-first-aether-vanguard-match-choose-two-lanes-to-win)



For other AI-assisted game developers: how do you keep test activity out of your acquisition numbers when agents and people use the same build?
